title: multi-gpu-parallelism-performance-study-wip
summary: Working notes and preliminary results from multi-GPU parallelism performance experiments. Focus is on tensor vs pipeline parallelism tradeoffs, NCCL behavior, and interconnect limits (PCIe/NVLink/IB). Goal: identify dominant bottlenecks for typical inference-serving workloads and recommend mitigations for the runtime.
objective: Characterize end-to-end inference throughput and latency when scaling a transformer model across multiple GPUs using common parallelism strategies. Pinpoint where wall-clock time is spent (compute vs. communication vs. CPU overhead) and produce actionable mitigations and configuration recommendations for Redwood serving runtime.
environment_setup: Hardware: single-node DGX A100 (8xA100-80GB) and 2-node cluster of rtx-6000-class machines connected with RoCEv2-enabled 100Gb IB for multi-node tests. OS: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.x, NCCL 2.18. Runtime: Redwood serving-runtime branch 'multi-gpu-experiments'. Models: GPT-like decoder-only models: 2B (24 layers), 7B (32 layers) FP16 and int8-quantized variants. Batch shapes: single-request streaming (batch=1), batched inference (batch=8, 16, 32).
methodology: 1) Implemented two parallelism modes in the test harness: tensor-parallel (shard large linear/kernel ops across GPUs) and pipeline-parallel (layer-wise partitioning). 2) Controlled variables: total batch size, sequence length, number of micro-batches for pipeline. 3) Measured per-request p95 latency and sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and captured detailed traces with Nsight Systems + NCCL logging. 4) Microbenchmarks: NCCL allreduce/allgather bandwidth and latency tests, PCIe peer-to-peer throughput (p2p bandwidth), and CPU->GPU memcpy timings. 5) Repeated runs to capture variability and cold vs warm cache behavior.
profiling_tools_and_flags: Nsight Systems (sys profile), Nsight Compute (kernel-level), nvprof deprecated; use CUPTI/NVTX markers instrumented in runtime. NCCL tests used 'nccl-tests' repo (all_reduce, all_gather, all_to_all) and NCCL logging enabled with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0. Key env vars: NCCL_P2P_LEVEL, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME, NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL, CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0 for baseline and 1 for debug. Collected perf counters for SM utilization, achieved occupancy, memory throughput, and kernel durations.
experiments_and_results: Experiment A: Single-node scaling 1->8 GPUs (DGX A100), model 7B FP16, batch=8, seq_len=512. - Tensor-parallel (1D sharding) achieved near-linear scaling 1->4 GPUs (45-70% speedup per extra GPU) but diminishing returns 4->8 due to NCCL allreduce overhead on attention/kv caches and frequent small all-reduces for optimizer-inference syncs. - Pipeline-parallel across 4 stages (2 GPUs per stage) improved throughput vs single-GPU for large batches but increased p95 latency for single-request traffic due to micro-batching and pipeline fill/drain. Experiment B: Multi-node scaling (2 nodes x4 gpus) using RoCE. - Observed ~2.1x throughput scaling from 4->8 GPUs for batch workloads but high tail latency spikes correlated with IB retransmits (NCCL logs showed IB flakiness). Enabling GPUDirect RDMA and tuning MTU reduced retransmits and improved stability. Microbenchmark: NCCL allreduce on 8 GPUs: practical bandwidth ~70% of theoretical on NVLink mesh for medium-sized messages (1MB), but for many small messages (<64KB) latency dominated and collective overheads prevented scaling. PCIe p2p tests showed host-staging fallback when NVLink paths not used (topology binding issue).
key_findings: - Communication dominates as we scale past 4 GPUs for the studied model shapes: frequent small collectives (attention KV exchanges, attention score reductions) cause high per-step overhead. - Pipeline-parallelism can improve throughput with large batching and sufficient micro-batches, but hurts single-request latency; useful for throughput-oriented Dedicated mode but not for low-latency Hosted API without request coalescing. - NCCL topology awareness matters: incorrect NCCL P2P selection or OS iface configuration can force PCIe-host roundtrips, killing bandwidth. - NIC layer instability (IB retransmits) explains severe tail latency in multi-node setups; requires RDMA and careful NIC configuration. - Kernel inefficiencies (small GEMMs, many small launches) lead to low SM utilization; fusing and custom kernels regain headroom.
profiling_artifacts_summary: Collected artifacts: Nsight Systems traces for representative runs (1G,4G,8G), NCCL logs for all runs, kernel flamegraphs from Nsight Compute, and nccl-tests CSV outputs. Observed recurring timeline patterns: (1) bursts of short-duration kernels separated by NCCL collective phases; (2) CPU-side scheduling gaps where CUDA streams were starved due to synchronous host operations; (3) NVLink hops visible in NCCL topology logs when NVLink mesh exploited (DGX) vs PCIe fallback on generic servers.
recommendations_and_action_items: - Runtime: add optional communication-computation overlap paths (async NCCL calls + CUDA streams) and increase aggregation of small tensors into larger collectives to reduce call overhead. - Orchestration: prefer NVLink-enabled nodes for 4+ GPU serving; advertise topology constraints and avoid arbitrary packing that forces PCIe fallbacks. - NCCL tuning: set NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL, explicitly configure NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME for correct IB iface, and prefer GPUDirect RDMA for multi-node. - Model: where feasible, prefer tensor sharding that reduces allreduce frequency (e.g., fused KV caches) and increase micro-batch count for pipeline to amortize fill/drain. - Monitoring: surface NCCL retry/retransmit metrics and per-request breakdown (compute vs comm vs CPU) in Redwood Console to detect multi-node instabilities early. Action items: 1) Implement fused-collectives prototype in runtime (Evan). 2) Add NCCL topology validation check during node allocation (Priya). 3) Run extended multi-node stress tests with RDMA tuning (Miguel).
known_limitations_and_open_questions: - Tests biased to decoder-only models; encoder-decoder and very long context lengths might shift bottlenecks. - Int8/quantized kernels sometimes change kernel shapes causing different collectives; need repeat experiments for quantized flows. - We need to test across other interconnects (Mellanox CX6/7 variations) and cloud instances (AWS p4d/p5, GCP A2) as topology and driver stacks differ. - How much of the observed small-message overhead can be mitigated by batching at the API layer without harming tail latency?
next_steps: 1) Prototype async NCCL-based overlap and run A/B vs baseline on 8-GPU DGX. 2) Add automatic topology validation during job placement and fail fast when NVLink not available for a requested config. 3) Re-run experiments for 2B model and int8 flows. 4) Add per-request telemetry export to Console for communication vs compute split. 5) Draft a playbook for Dedicated customers recommending node types and NCCL tuning values.
raw_logs_note: Raw trace files and nccl-tests CSVs are large and stored in internal artifact storage (linked in Confluence). Keep this doc as the explainer and pointer to artifacts.
authors_note: This is a working document: expect iterative updates. Tagging Evan, Priya, Miguel for follow-up. If you run additional experiments, add a short note under 'experiments_and_results' with date and key deltas.
conclusion: Multi-GPU scaling for inference is feasible and provides strong throughput gains, but is frequently communication-limited beyond moderate GPU counts. Practical wins will come from (1) reducing the frequency/number of small collectives, (2) overlapping comm and compute, (3) ensuring hardware/topology matches the planned parallelism strategy. For Hosted low-latency traffic, prefer single- or small-scale sharding and invest in aggressive caching/batching; for Dedicated throughput contracts, pipeline+tensor combos with NVLink nodes and RDMA are the sweet spot.
